rows.title_short: Workers' Compensation Act of 2005
rows.abstract: \"Workers' Compensation Act of 2005\". The bill proposes a comprehensive and integrated implementation of the employees' compensation program that focuses not only on benefits payment but also on work contingency prevention and, in situations where workers would eventually suffer from work-connected sickness or injury, their rehabilitation into productive members of society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-03-08

rows.author: C018
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A WORKING TIME FLEXIBILIZATION IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES, THEREBY AMENDING ARTICLES 83, 85, AND 87 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE FOUR HUNDRED FORTY-TWO (PD 442), AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The bill provides for a shortened or compressed work week by extending normal daily working hours but not to exceed 10 hours a day.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-03-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE JURISDICTION OF LABOR CASES BETWEEN THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION (NLRC) AND THE REGIONAL OFFICES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT (DOLE), AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE, ARTICLES 128 AND 217 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBER FOUR HUNDRED FORTY-TWO (PD 442), AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to transfer the jurisdiction over labor cases from the National Labor Relations Commission to the regional offices of the Department of Labor and Employment REGARDLESS OF THE AMOUNT OF CLAIM.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-03-08

rows.author: C018

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE EXCEPTIONS FROM THE NIGHT WORK PROHIBITION OF WOMEN EMPLOYEES, THEREBY AMENDING ARTICLE 131 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBER FOUR HUNDRED AND FORTY-TWO (PD 442), AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: To allow more women to work during nighttime, the bill seeks to lift certain prohibitions identified in Article 131 of the Labor Code, such as: a) in cases of emergency; b) in case of urgent work performed on machineries, equipment or installation, and c) where work is necessary to prevent the serious loss of perishable goods.
